fichas.title: Dung and slurry production and drainage
fichas.summary: Farm-animal dung and urine production varies with animal type, live weight, fodder and drink. The page describes average solid-dung and slurry production, storage considerations, and regulations concerning pollution risks and watercourses.
uses: Collecting and storing animal dung, urine and cleaning water
Reducing pollution from farmyard drainage and manure storage

dimensions.context: Definition of one large animal unit (LU).

dimensions.label: Straw litter quantity
dimensions.context: Normal litter quantity associated with solid dung.
dimensions.ocr_raw: The normal litter quantity of 1.5–2 kg of straw per LU/day

dimensions.label: Solid dung stacking height
dimensions.context: Stacking height resulting from the normal litter quantity.
dimensions.ocr_raw: results in a stacking height of solid dung of 2.0–2.5 m

dimensions.label: Dung slab area
dimensions.context: Area equivalent given for solid-dung storage.
dimensions.ocr_raw: equivalent to a dung slab of 0.5 m²/LU × month

dimensions.label: Assumed dung area for storage period
dimensions.context: Assumption corresponding to six months’ storage, used in the solid-dung discussion.
dimensions.ocr_raw: 3 m² dung per LU is assumed (corresponds to 6 months’ storage)

dimensions.label: Solid-dung-related slurry production
dimensions.context: Slurry production stated under the solid-dung discussion, with rainwater contribution assumed.
dimensions.ocr_raw: this gives slurry production of 0.64 m³/LU × month

dimensions.label: Free space above highest slurry level
dimensions.context: Suggested free space in open slurry tanks to take rainwater.
dimensions.ocr_raw: a free space of 20–30 cm above the highest slurry level

dimensions.label: Milk-cow slurry production
dimensions.context: Approximate slurry production for milk cows.
dimensions.ocr_raw: Milk cows produce about 1.4 m³/LU × month of slurry.

dimensions.label: Bullock slurry production with maize silage
dimensions.context: Approximate production under intensive fattening with maize silage fodder.
dimensions.ocr_raw: can reduce slurry production to about 1.0 m³/LU × month

dimensions.label: Watercourse separation
dimensions.context: Minimum location distance from watercourses specified in the cited England and Wales regulations.
dimensions.ocr_raw: they may not be located within 10 m of watercourses that might become polluted

fichas.title: Farmyard dung and slurry storage systems
fichas.summary: Illustrated options for storing and removing solid dung and slurry include underground and earth tanks, overground tanks with pumping arrangements, dung stores above or beside slurry pits, and front or side access arrangements. The diagrams identify components and a few construction and layout dimensions.
uses: Separating or combining solid-dung storage and slurry collection
